evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: No other story duplicates the specific requirement to create a new game with name and optional description.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: No other story expresses the same invitation-via-URL requirement or duplicates this functionality.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: No other story specifies starting a round via entering an item in a single multi-line text field.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: This moderator view of all items in the session is distinct (actor/context) from other stories.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item to be estimated/re-estimated is a distinct moderator action; related re-estimate story exists but differs in phrasing and intent.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding items to the list is a unique CRUD requirement not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing items is a distinct requirement; no other story duplicates this exact operation.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting items is a specific operation and not duplicated by other stories.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: This moderator ability to show estimates before all estimators have responded is distinct from other reveal behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting the average is a specific moderation decision not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: have the "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Automatic filling of the estimate when unanimous is a distinct automated behaviour.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Manual entry of the agreed estimate is distinct from auto-fill or accepting averages.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Substantially overlaps with PP-005 which allows selecting an item to be re-estimated; both express the same moderator re-estimation requirement.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories programmatically from a spreadsheet is a distinct requirement from copy/paste.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste as a user action is a different mechanism than import; not a duplicate per the criterion.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games is distinct from scrolling through prior rounds or viewing transcripts.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a transcript is different from exporting it or browsing games; no exact duplicate exists.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Export to HTML is a specific output format requirement distinct from viewing or CSV export.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Export to CSV is a specific requirement distinct from other transcript operations.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game and its data is a distinct administrative action not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Account creation with these fields is unique and not duplicated by other stories.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Login is a distinct authentication requirement separate from account creation or password reminders.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Updating account details is a separate operation from creation, deletion, or login.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Account deletion is a distinct requirement; no duplicate story specifying the same action exists.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display for dates/times is a unique presentation requirement not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder via email is a distinct recovery mechanism not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Choosing the card scale is a particular configuration requirement distinct from other features.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: A limit on number of invitees is a different requirement than the invitation mechanism; not duplicated.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via the game URL and entering name is distinct from invitation and other flows.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Estimator view of the current item is a unique requirement distinct from moderator actions.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Estimator perspective on seeing all session items is distinct from the moderator version (PP-004) because the actor differs.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Immediate indicator that someone has given an estimate is distinct from viewing revealed estimates or lists of who gave what.

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: This synchronized reveal behavior is distinct and not duplicated by other stories that allow early reveals.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: This participant-level timing rule for changing estimates is a specific requirement; the duplicate story (PP-041) repeats it.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Showing prior estimates per estimator is a unique historical-tracking requirement.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Displaying who gave which estimate in the current round is distinct from indicating whether someone has given an estimate.

evaluations.evidence: be able start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared countdown timer is a specific feature and not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: have the two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Automatic timer reset behavior tied to play events is a distinct requirement from starting the timer.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling through prior rounds within a session is different from browsing previous games or viewing transcripts.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Maintaining card order across draws is a unique UI consistency requirement.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: This participant ability to change estimates duplicates PP-034 which already specifies changing up until the last person selects; no meaningful difference in actor or context.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a thumbnail near played cards is a specific personalization UI feature not repeated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: have written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: General standards compliance is distinct from browser-specific compatibility or accessibility requirements.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Providing a glossary is a specific documentation requirement not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Creating database indexes is a distinct developer performance task not duplicated in the backlog.

evaluations.evidence: have the application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Specifying support for specific old browsers is a distinct compatibility requirement not duplicated by general standards compliance.

evaluations.evidence: have the site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance requirement is unique and not duplicated by other developer stories.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: A general performance/UX responsiveness requirement is distinct and not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a distinct internationalization requirement not duplicated by other stories.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design/readability is a distinct usability requirement; no duplicate exists.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Custom/error page design is a unique UX requirement not duplicated elsewhere.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Anonymized/non-identifiable storage for research is a specific privacy requirement not duplicated by other stories.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Collecting/displaying usage metrics for an administrator (Mike) is a unique reporting requirement.
